summary: Item 'tiers' finished after the independent review. An earlier fix run had been cut off by a container restart. Its patch (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Struthio/62270cd8-8155-590e-b29e-91307882a142/scratchpad/work/b084b/tiers.patch, 23:18) already held every review fix and applied cleanly to this worktree (wf_401c7b30-522-12). I read tools/run_tiers.py and the new tests again against each finding and all are there. Must fix 1: a Stop object catches SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGHUP while the run lasts (signals the shell ignores stay ignored). Worker threads are daemons. Every running child is killed with its process group, and its HOME and TMPDIR folders are removed. The rows are marked INTERRUPTED or NOT RUN, tier<N>.json is still written, and the exit code is 128 plus the signal number (130 for Ctrl-C). Each child also runs under `timeout -s KILL` at its limit plus 30 s, as a backstop if the run itself is killed. Must fix 2: changed_files uses --no-renames, so a moved file counts under both names. All 13 should_fix items are done (listed under decisions). I then re-tested on a fresh copy and re-measured. test_run_tiers, test_release_check and test_machine pass in both looks. Tier 0 had 0 failing in both looks. Tier 2 in both looks as one run: 25 min 3 s, 196 runs, 2,302 tests, 0 failing, 10 skipped, all named. The one mutation the earlier run had not re-checked is now caught, so 12 of 12 are caught. I updated the measured times in docs/CHECKS.md and rewrote the patch, which applies to a clean export of HEAD. One thing outside this item: test_rail_demo writes .pyc files into workbench/view_modules even under -B. I did not fix it (see not_done).

decisions: I applied the cut-off fixer's patch as it was. Regenerated from the worktree, it is byte-identical to the saved one. I did not rewrite fixes that were already done and sound.

All of the program's own variables are dropped by prefix (ARC_LEDGER_, ARC1_WORKBENCH_, LEDGER_, GRAPHITE_), not by a fixed list. GRAPHITE_HOST_MEMORY_LIMIT and GRAPHITE_CAMPAIGN_FIXTURES from the owner's shell therefore do not reach tests either. A run's result should not depend on the shell it was started from. The capture-folder variable for a window check is added after the filtering.
Graphite's look runs with GRAPHITE_APPEARANCE unset, the house default; Kasandra's sets it. tiers 0 and 1 still default to the look in force in the shell when --look is not given.

A tier 2 unit stopped by an interrupt counts as failing, and the last line starts with 'interrupted, N of M not run'. Skipped tests do not make a run fail, but they are counted in each row, shown in the table, and named on the last line.

Non-Python changed files are matched by file name on a word boundary, not by relative path. Tests refer to the root README.md as 'README.md', so matching the path would not shrink the set. Tier 1 still chooses more than it needs to for a README edit, and that errs on the safe side.

Tier 2 was measured as one run in both looks rather than once per look. The builder had already measured each look separately, and the doc only had an estimate for the combined run, which is the default.
I did not fix the .pyc that test_rail_demo leaves in workbench/view_modules. It comes from the program or a test, not the runner, and it is outside this item.
not_done: test_rail_demo, run alone through run_all in Graphite's look (with -B and PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 in its environment), leaves 7 .pyc files in workbench/view_modules/__pycache__ of the copy. Running test_one_name the same way leaves none. The likely cause is the Kernel's job environment: workbench/engineering_kernel.py builds it from an allow-list of os.environ and sets PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE only in the snapshot branch, around line 1455. I did not trace it further or fix it. The review's 'nothing written into the program' check used git status, which does not show ignored __pycache__ folders.

Tier 0 is under 60 s every time, but on a busy machine the margin is small: 52 s with another build's tests running beside it. If it must hold under load, the cheapest saving is to run test_one_name's code classes in two parts (15 s in this run).

release_note: Checks now come in tiers, all run with one command: tools/run_tiers.py. Tier 0 runs in under a minute after every change and always includes the tests that guard you. Tier 1 adds the tests that use the files you changed, including files that were moved or renamed. Tier 2 is the release check: every test, every window check, the playable scene on Rail Demo and the name sweep, in both looks, in about 25 minutes, ending in one table and one line, '0 failing' or what failed, with any skipped tests named. Each test runs alone with its own empty home folder and cannot leave anything running behind it, and Ctrl-C stops a run at once and still saves what it found.
